data.ruling: The refutation stands. The value's step "the two shunt paths replace each other, so one INA228 answers per test" does not follow from its sources. The owner's rule (IOBoard.md:442) is that a test is cabled through one shunt path, never both. It says nothing about which monitor is on the bus. Under F1 (owner, 2026-09-25) and IOBoard.md:503, the board carries two INA228s, one for each path, with no switch in a sense path. Each has its own A0/A1 address on the measurement coprocessor's I2C bus. The INA228 datasheet makes the address acknowledge depend only on the A0/A1 pin states and a valid address byte, not on what IN+, IN- or VBUS are wired to. So both powered INA228s answer in every test, and the rule "the monitor whenever it answers" cannot pick the cabled path. That makes the value incomplete as a rule for filling BENCH page 0x20 registers 0 and 1. A secondary point: the tree already has a selector, a single ina228_en setting and a one-address ina228_addr setting (0x40, 0x41, 0x44 or 0x45). IOBoard.md:503 says that setting "takes one address". So "how the firmware tells which path is cabled is not stated" overlooks the configured address. The confirmed parts of the value still hold: on the bring-up module the ESC telemetry is the only voltage and current source (main.c), and the ESC's figures and the shunt are independent measurements (OpenYGE.md:380-381). The finding is about this function's requirement value (V154, Motor monitor), not about the INA228 part, so its scope is function.
data.evidence: Datasheet SLYS021A (Rev. A, May 2022), 7.5.1: "The device has two address pins, A0 and A1. Table 7-2 lists the pin logic levels for each of the 16 possible addresses. The device samples the state of pins A0 and A1 on every bus communication." 7.5.1.1: "This byte is the secondary device address, with the R/W bit low. The device then acknowledges receipt of a valid address." Neither section makes the acknowledge depend on the shunt or bus inputs. Checkout 68adf31: hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:442: "The two paths replace each other: a test is cabled through one of them, never both (owner, 2026-09-25)." IOBoard.md:503 (Motor monitor address): "two INA228, one for each shunt path (F1), each set by its A0 and A1 pins to its own address. The display's INA228 address setting offers 0x40, 0x41, 0x44 and 0x45 and takes one address". Research.md:678, F1, owner's answer: "one INA238 for each path (owner, 2026-09-25)"; the proposed answer there reads "no switch sits in a sense path, and the firmware reads whichever is wired. The two positions differ by I2C address". Research.md:707 applies V154 to the INA228. shared/settings/settings.c:29 has k_ina_addr = {"0x40","0x41","0x44","0x45"}. settings.c:87-95 defines SET_INA228_EN ("ina228_en"), SET_INA228_ADDR ("ina228_addr", "Set by its A0 and A1 pins", one enum value) and SET_INA228_SHUNT. firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:714-727 has the comment "There is no other source for any of these on this board" and fills voltage and current only from extended DShot telemetry (EDT).
